title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: additive Cheon with planned pair walks and native-offset cluster matching

claims.statement:
For the protected BLS12-381 G1 target with auxiliary powers and every n with 2^20 <= n < r, the algorithm in proof.md recovers s with heuristic success probability at least 0.398 (required 0.39) over the uniform challenge and fresh algorithm coins. It is Cheon's attack in the subgroup H of 2^20-th powers (d = 2^20 divides r-1, 6d divides r-1, A_d is read; only A_1 and A_d are used). Baby and giant scalars are products a*b in H with a a prime of (2^76, 2^76 + 2^70] taken in increasing order and b a class integer <= 2^76 with chi(b) = -chi(a). One algorithmic change over the one-addition-per-point architecture: each class list is planned offline into three-term progressions (x-g, x, x+g) with g <= 2^44 = 16 d^2, and the walk computes [a(x+g)]Q = P+T and [a(x-g)]Q = P-T from the stored midpoint P = [ax]Q and the table entry T = [ag]Q with one shared field inversion, priced as one reference addition plus three extra field multiplications: 2000 + 3*383 = 3149 instructions for two points plus charged second-formula arithmetic; the planned pair fraction is at least f = 0.98 (heuristic H4, measured 0.9815-0.9862 on real toy class lists at matched ratios). Records are 32-byte truncated 192-bit U-orbit keys, matched in direct-mapped head arrays chained through pools at 2^60 owner nodes, moved by two hops of 4 KiB blocks through balanced-fan-in relays (every receiver has
exactly 2^10 senders) using dedicated per-pair receive rings in which every word has exactly
one writer (sender-written ring slots and sequence words, receiver-written credit words); a
targeted software-generated interrupt wakes the receiver, whose handler sweeps its 2^10
sequence words and drains every pair that advanced (wakes and sweeps are charged ledger
rows), so correctness never depends on identifying the interrupting sender; the sender pays
the block stores and post control, the receiver the wake, sweep, reads and credit returns,
with the memory-ordering barriers charged; no remote-memory instruction, no device work, no
locks or atomics, every byte written and read exactly once and charged, and an idle node
executes nothing until its interrupt; candidates are resolved by one bounded linear re-walk of each chain and at most 96 scalar tests, all charged. Total work W(2^20) is at most 2^116.538377 target-group-operation equivalents (exact score 116538377/1000000), including both walks and their gap tables, matching and comparisons, transport, plan construction and streaming, the character sieves and base search, candidate handling, the d-th root, the mu_d search and input access. Preprocessing (challenge-independent work) is at most 2^115.5276 units and is included. Peak memory is at most 2^122.6439 bytes; there is no nonuniform advice. Heuristics, all disclosed in proof.md with toy evidence at its stated scope: H1 (coverage |R|/m >= 1 - e^{-K} - 0.0005 at the realized K >= 0.51, supported by an exact census of the construction on toy primes up to m = 2^32 in which every modular and rational coincidence is measured, never excluded by size; the census machinery is validated against independent brute-force field arithmetic), H2 (character equidistribution, affecting only charged small terms, with a stop-and-fail rule), H3 (keys as uniform strings, with every cap and tail bounded and overflow counted as failure), H4 (pair fraction >= 0.98), H5 (Poisson-like candidate multiplicity, with the total-candidate tails at the exact unconditional mean N^2/2^192 + N^2/M and the per-run true-hit multiplicity Markov-bounded at its conditional mean 1.28, supported by an exact second-moment census diagnostic that reads 1.000 at k = 12). This is an analytic bound with itemised instruction counts, not a full-size execution.

experiments.purpose: One run with five parts. (1) ledger: recomputes every cost term of proof.md section 6 from exact integers, the exact score with its boundary assert, the preprocessing and memory inequalities, the success inequality with every failure term, and the production algebra identities; arithmetic only. (2) planner: the offline pairing planner of proof.md section 3 on real chi-class lists of toy primes at the production degree parameter GMAX = 16 d^2, sweeping the list span; reports pair fraction, cycle rejections, dependency depth against the cap (evidence for H4). (3) ec: the whole algorithm on a toy j = 0 curve with 2 not in H: planned paired walk with the shared-inversion pair formula, ordered disjoint bases, truncated-key bucket matching with false matches counted, bounded re-walk, six-z resolution, d-th root and mu_d scan; success against prediction, every recovered scalar verified, every sampled collision event checked against the exact coverage of the independently reconstructed emitted sets. (4) proto: the section-4 transport protocol under an adversarial scheduler — 32 producers x 16 blocks through dedicated depth-8 rings, sequence words and credit words, wake-only interrupts with coalescing on the 16 shared interrupt ids, sweep-based handlers; 60 schedules, every record delivered exactly once (and the same simulation detects both rejected flaw classes: the shared-counter queue records 2841 partial-id reads, and identify-by-interrupt-source loses 15360 blocks when producers exceed the 16 interrupt ids). (5) census: the exact coverage |R|/m of the construction on a toy prime at the production scaling rule, with the exact multiplicity diagnostic (evidence for H1 and H5). Toy parts are evidence at toy/simulation scope only.
